title: Cognitive Set 01: Core Ascend Simulation
description: Balanced medium-hard set covering pipes, boats, mixture replacement, DI ratios, circular seating, syllogisms, and original RC passage.

questions.question: Pipe A can fill an overhead tank in 12 hours and Pipe B can fill it in 15 hours, while an outlet Pipe C can empty the full tank in 20 hours. Pipes A and B are opened together for 4 hours, after which Pipe C is also opened. How many total hours from the start will it take to fill the tank completely?
questions.explanation: Take tank capacity = LCM(12, 15, 20) = 60 units. Filling rates: A = +5 u/hr, B = +4 u/hr, C = -3 u/hr. In the first 4 hours, A and B fill 4 * (5 + 4) = 36 units. Remaining = 60 - 36 = 24 units. With C open, net rate = 5 + 4 - 3 = 6 u/hr. Additional time = 24 / 6 = 4 hours. Total time = 4 + 4 = 8 hours.
questions.shortcut: Use LCM(12,15,20)=60 units; 36 units done in 4h leaves 24 units at net +6/h = 4h more.

questions.question: A motorboat travels 36 km upstream and 48 km downstream in 10 hours. On another trip on the same river, it covers 24 km upstream and 60 km downstream in 9 hours. What is the speed of the river current?
questions.explanation: Let upstream speed = u and downstream speed = d. Equations: 36/u + 48/d = 10 and 24/u + 60/d = 9. Multiply first by 2 and second by 3: 72/u + 96/d = 20 and 72/u + 180/d = 27. Subtracting gives 84/d = 7, so d = 12 km/h. Substituting d = 12 into 36/u + 4 = 10 gives 36/u = 6, so u = 6 km/h. Stream speed = (d - u)/2 = (12 - 6)/2 = 3 km/h.
questions.shortcut: Test clean factors of 36 and 48: u=6, d=12 satisfies 6+4=10 and 4+5=9 immediately.

questions.question: A container holds 80 litres of pure milk. Sixteen litres of milk are drawn out and replaced with water. This exact replacement operation is performed one more time, and finally 10 litres of pure water are poured into the container. What is the final ratio of milk to water?
questions.explanation: After two replacements of 16 L out of 80 L (fraction 1/5), remaining milk = 80 * (1 - 1/5)^2 = 80 * (16/25) = 51.2 L. Water before final addition = 80 - 51.2 = 28.8 L. After adding 10 L pure water, water = 38.8 L. Ratio = 51.2 : 38.8 = 512 : 388 = 128 : 97.
questions.shortcut: Milk = 80*(4/5)^2 = 51.2 L; total volume becomes 90 L, so water = 38.8 L; divide both by 0.4.

questions.question: The difference between compound interest (compounded annually) and simple interest on a certain principal at 10% per annum for 3 years is Rs. 930. What is the principal amount?
questions.explanation: For 3 years at rate r%, CI - SI = P * (r/100)^2 * (3 + r/100). At r = 10%, factor = 0.01 * 3.1 = 0.031. Therefore P = 930 / 0.031 = Rs. 30,000.
questions.shortcut: At 10% for 3 years, SI = 30% and CI = 33.1%, so 3.1% of P = 930 => P = 30,000.

questions.question: How many distinct 5-digit numbers divisible by 4 can be formed using the digits {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6} if no digit may be repeated?
questions.explanation: A number is divisible by 4 iff its last two digits form a number divisible by 4. From {1,2,3,4,5,6} without repetition, valid two-digit endings are: 12, 16, 24, 32, 36, 52, 56, 64 (8 choices). The remaining 3 places can be filled from the remaining 4 digits in 4 * 3 * 2 = 24 ways. Total = 8 * 24 = 192.
questions.shortcut: Count valid 2-digit endings divisible by 4 without repeat (8) and multiply by 4P3 (24).

questions.question: Urn X contains 4 red and 6 blue balls. Urn Y contains 5 red and 5 blue balls. One ball is drawn at random from Urn X and placed into Urn Y without noting its colour. Then one ball is drawn from Urn Y. What is the probability that the ball drawn from Urn Y is red?
questions.explanation: Case 1: Red ball transferred from X (prob 4/10); Urn Y now has 6R, 5B, so P(Red) = 6/11. Case 2: Blue ball transferred from X (prob 6/10); Urn Y now has 5R, 6B, so P(Red) = 5/11. Total P(Red) = (4/10)*(6/11) + (6/10)*(5/11) = (24 + 30)/110 = 54/110 = 27/55.

questions.question: Two trains of lengths 180 m and 220 m travel on parallel tracks. Running in opposite directions, they cross each other in 10 seconds. Running in the same direction, the faster train completely overtakes the slower train in 40 seconds. Find the speed of the faster train in km/h.
questions.explanation: Total crossing distance = 180 + 220 = 400 m. Opposite direction: v1 + v2 = 400/10 = 40 m/s. Same direction: v1 - v2 = 400/40 = 10 m/s. Adding gives 2*v1 = 50 => v1 = 25 m/s = 25 * (18/5) = 90 km/h.

questions.question: A merchant marks his goods 40% above cost price and offers two successive discounts of 15% and 10%. While selling, he uses a tampered balance that weighs 900 g instead of 1 kg. What is his actual net profit percentage?
questions.explanation: Assume CP of 1000 g = Rs. 1000 (Rs. 1/g). Actual cost of 900 g delivered = Rs. 900. Marked price for nominal 1 kg = Rs. 1400. Selling price after 15% and 10% discounts = 1400 * 0.85 * 0.90 = Rs. 1071. Profit = 1071 - 900 = Rs. 171 on Rs. 900 => (171/900)*100 = 19%.

questions.passage:
Delivery Centre Metrics (FY24 vs FY25):
- Noida: FY24 Rev Rs 420 Cr (1,400 staff) | FY25 Rev Rs 504 Cr (1,600 staff)
- Chennai: FY24 Rev Rs 600 Cr (2,000 staff) | FY25 Rev Rs 690 Cr (2,300 staff)
- Bengaluru: FY24 Rev Rs 750 Cr (2,500 staff) | FY25 Rev Rs 945 Cr (2,700 staff)
- Pune: FY24 Rev Rs 330 Cr (1,100 staff) | FY25 Rev Rs 396 Cr (1,200 staff)
questions.question: Based on the Delivery Centre table, which two centres achieved the exact same percentage growth in revenue from FY24 to FY25?
questions.explanation: Noida growth = (504 - 420)/420 = 84/420 = 20%. Chennai = 90/600 = 15%. Bengaluru = (945 - 750)/750 = 195/750 = 26%. Pune = (396 - 330)/330 = 66/330 = 20%. Thus Noida and Pune both grew by exactly 20%.

questions.passage:
Delivery Centre Metrics (FY24 vs FY25):
- Noida: FY24 Rev Rs 420 Cr (1,400 staff) | FY25 Rev Rs 504 Cr (1,600 staff)
- Chennai: FY24 Rev Rs 600 Cr (2,000 staff) | FY25 Rev Rs 690 Cr (2,300 staff)
- Bengaluru: FY24 Rev Rs 750 Cr (2,500 staff) | FY25 Rev Rs 945 Cr (2,700 staff)
- Pune: FY24 Rev Rs 330 Cr (1,100 staff) | FY25 Rev Rs 396 Cr (1,200 staff)
questions.question: Using the Delivery Centre Metrics above (with Bengaluru FY25 revenue = Rs 945 Cr), what is the overall revenue per employee (in Rs Lakhs) across all 4 centres combined in FY25?
questions.explanation: Total FY25 revenue = 504 + 690 + 945 + 396 = 2535 Cr = 253,500 Lakhs. Total FY25 staff = 1600 + 2300 + 2700 + 1200 = 7800. Revenue per employee = 253,500 / 7,800 = 32.5 Lakhs.
questions.shortcut: Sum revenues (2535 Cr) and staff (7800); 2535 * 100 / 7800 = 32.5 Lakhs.

questions.question: Eight engineers P, Q, R, S, T, U, V, and W sit around a circular table facing the center. P sits second to the right of T, who is third to the right of R. S sits second to the left of V, and V is not an immediate neighbor of P or T. U sits opposite W, and U is not an immediate neighbor of P. Who sits immediately to the left of U?
questions.explanation: Number seats 1..8 counter-clockwise (right = +1, left = -1). Set T=1 => P=3 (2nd right). T is 3rd right of R => R=6. V is not adjacent to T(1) or P(3), so V is 5 or 7. S is 2nd left of V; if V=5 then S=3 (occupied by P), so V=7 and S=5. Remaining seats {2,4,8} belong to U, W, Q. Only 4 and 8 are opposite, so {U,W}={4,8} and Q=2. Since U is not adjacent to P(3), U=8 and W=4. Immediately left (-1) of U(8) is seat 7, which is V.
questions.shortcut: Fix T=1, P=3, R=6; force V=7, S=5; opposite pair {4,8} with U not near P(3) puts U=8, so left of U is V.

questions.question: Statements: (1) All microservices are containers. (2) Some containers are pods. (3) No pod is a monolith. Conclusions: I. Some containers are not monoliths. II. All monoliths being microservices is a possibility.
questions.explanation: From (2) and (3), the containers that are pods cannot be monoliths, so Conclusion I definitely follows. For Conclusion II, there is no negative restriction between monoliths and microservices (only pod and monolith are disjoint), so a Venn diagram where all monoliths lie inside microservices (outside pods) is completely valid. Hence both I and II follow.
questions.shortcut: Check negative boundary: only Pod <-> Monolith is blocked; Containers overlapping Pods proves I, and Monoliths inside Microservices-only zone is valid for II.

questions.question: If A + B means A is the mother of B; A - B means A is the brother of B; A * B means A is the father of B; and A / B means A is the sister of B, then which expression proves that P is the maternal uncle of S?
questions.explanation: For P to be the maternal uncle of S, P must be male and the brother of S's mother. In 'P - M + S / N': P is the brother of M (P is male), M is the mother of S, and S is the sister of N. Thus P is M's brother and M is S's mother, making P the maternal uncle of S.
questions.shortcut: Need P - MotherOf(S): only option C has P - M followed directly by M + S.

questions.question: In a certain cipher, SPRING is coded as HPJTQU and ORACLE is coded as FNDCSQ. How is DEPLOY coded in the same cipher?
questions.explanation: Reverse the 6-letter word, then add +1, +2, +1, +2, +1, +2 alternately to the letters. SPRING reversed is GNIRPS; shifting (+1,+2,+1,+2,+1,+2) yields H, P, J, T, Q, U. DEPLOY reversed is YOLPED; shifting (+1,+2,+1,+2,+1,+2) gives Y+1=Z, O+2=Q, L+1=M, P+2=R, E+1=F, D+2=F => ZQMRFF.
questions.shortcut: Reverse word first, then apply alternating +1/+2 shifts: Y+1=Z, O+2=Q, L+1=M.

questions.question: What is the value of the two-digit positive integer N? Statement I: The sum of the digits of N is 9, and reversing the digits decreases the number by 27. Statement II: N is divisible by 9 and the tens digit is greater than the units digit.
options: Statement I alone is sufficient, while Statement II alone is not
Statement II alone is sufficient, while Statement I alone is not
Either Statement I alone or Statement II alone is sufficient
questions.explanation: From Statement I: Let N = 10x + y. x + y = 9 and (10x + y) - (10y + x) = 27 => 9(x - y) = 27 => x - y = 3. Solving gives x = 6, y = 3, so N = 63 uniquely. Statement II allows 54, 63, 72, 81, 90, so it is insufficient alone.
questions.shortcut: Difference of number and reverse = 9*(x-y), giving x-y=3 and x+y=9 => unique N=63.

questions.question: Find the missing term in the series: 7, 15, 32, 67, 138, ?
questions.explanation: Pattern: next = previous * 2 + k where k increments by 1 starting at 1: 7*2+1=15, 15*2+2=32, 32*2+3=67, 67*2+4=138, 138*2+5=281.
questions.shortcut: Each step is 2x + 1, 2x + 2, 2x + 3, 2x + 4, 2x + 5.

questions.question: A delivery drone flies 12 km North, turns right and flies 16 km, turns right and flies 24 km, turns left and flies 5 km, and finally turns left and flies 12 km. How far and in which direction is it from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Track (x, y) starting at (0,0): +12N => (0,12); right=East +16 => (16,12); right=South -24 => (16,-12); left=East +5 => (21,-12); left=North +12 => (21,0). Net displacement is 21 km East.
questions.shortcut: Net North-South = +12 - 24 + 12 = 0; Net East-West = +16 + 5 = 21 km East.

questions.question: Three candidates A, B, and C appear before a panel. Exactly one always lies while the other two always tell the truth. A says: 'B always tells the truth.' B says: 'Either A or C is the liar.' C says: 'A is the liar.' Who is the liar?
questions.explanation: Test each candidate as the sole liar: If A lies, then 'B tells the truth' is false, meaning B also lies (two liars—invalid). If B lies, then C tells the truth, so C's claim 'A is the liar' would be true (two liars—invalid). If C lies, then A and B tell the truth: A's claim about B is true, B's claim 'Either A or C is the liar' is true, and C's claim 'A is the liar' is false. Uniquely, C is the liar.
questions.shortcut: If A lied, B would also lie (since A endorses B). Thus A tells truth, B tells truth, leaving C as the liar.

questions.question: In a row of students, Ananya is 18th from the left end and Karthik is 23rd from the right end. When they interchange positions, Ananya becomes 29th from the left end. How many students are standing between Ananya and Karthik originally?
questions.explanation: Ananya moves from 18th to 29th from the left, meaning she moved 29 - 18 = 11 places right. Thus there are 11 - 1 = 10 students strictly between their original positions.
questions.shortcut: Between = |new_pos - old_pos| - 1 = |29 - 18| - 1 = 10.

questions.question: Five deployment tasks D1, D2, D3, D4, and D5 must run sequentially from Slot 1 to Slot 5. D1 runs immediately before D2, and D2 runs immediately before D4. D1 cannot run in Slot 1 or Slot 5. D3 must run at some point after D4. If D5 runs in Slot 1, which task MUST run in Slot 5?
questions.explanation: With D5 in Slot 1, slots 2–5 remain. The consecutive block D1-D2-D4 needs 3 adjacent slots from {2,3,4,5}, so it must occupy (2,3,4) or (3,4,5). Since D3 must run after D4, D4 cannot be in Slot 5. Thus D1=2, D2=3, D4=4, forcing D3 into Slot 5.
questions.shortcut: Block D1-D2-D4 followed by D3 leaves only [D5, D1, D2, D4, D3].

questions.passage: Enterprise software modernization rarely fails because organizations lack modern cloud tooling; it stalls when legacy business rules remain undocumented inside monolithic databases. Over decades, stored procedures absorb tax exceptions, regulatory overrides, and regional pricing quirks that no product backlog records. When engineering teams attempt a direct rewrite into microservices without first extracting an empirical behavior baseline from production traffic, subtle edge-case regressions emerge months after cutover. Consequently, disciplined migration programs invest heavily in shadow-traffic replay—routing mirrored live requests to both the legacy core and the new service—before retiring a single legacy table.
questions.question: According to the passage, why do direct microservice rewrites of legacy systems often suffer delayed regressions?
options: Cloud orchestration tools cannot handle high-volume regional pricing requests
Undocumented business exceptions remain embedded inside legacy database procedures
Shadow-traffic replay slows down production databases during cutover
Engineering teams refuse to retire obsolete database tables after migration
questions.explanation: The passage explicitly states that legacy business rules—tax exceptions, regulatory overrides, and regional quirks—accumulate inside stored procedures without documentation, causing subtle regressions if teams rewrite without baselining.
questions.shortcut: Locate 'subtle edge-case regressions emerge' and trace back to 'undocumented inside monolithic databases'.

Over decades, stored procedures absorb tax exceptions, regulatory overrides, and regional pricing quirks that no product backlog records. When engineering teams attempt a direct rewrite into microservices without first extracting an empirical behavior baseline from production traffic, subtle edge-case regressions emerge months after cutover. Consequently, disciplined migration programs invest heavily in shadow-traffic replay—routing mirrored live requests to both the legacy core and the new service—before retiring a single legacy table.
questions.question: What role does shadow-traffic replay serve in the migration strategy described?
options: It replaces the need for product backlogs entirely
It reduces cloud hosting costs prior to table retirement
It verifies behavioral parity between old and new services using real inputs
It automatically converts stored procedures into microservice endpoints
questions.explanation: Shadow-traffic replay routes mirrored live requests to both the legacy core and the new service to establish an empirical behavior baseline before retiring legacy tables.
questions.shortcut: Contrast 'empirical behavior baseline' + 'mirrored live requests to both' with the options.

questions.question: Identify the segment containing a grammatical error: 'Neither the lead architect (A) / nor the backend developers (B) / was informed about (C) / the sudden schema freeze. (D)'
questions.explanation: With 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject. Since 'the backend developers' is plural, segment (C) should read 'were informed about' instead of 'was informed about'.
questions.shortcut: Proximity rule for neither/nor: match verb to 'developers' (plural -> were).

questions.question:
Arrange sentences P, Q, R, S into a coherent paragraph:
P. However, this immediate speed gain often masks accumulating technical debt.
Q. Rapid prototyping allows startups to validate market demand within weeks.
R. Within a year, teams find that even minor feature additions trigger cascading failures.
S. Consequently, periodic refactoring sprints are essential to preserve velocity.
questions.explanation: Q introduces the topic ('Rapid prototyping'). P contrasts it ('this immediate speed gain'). R illustrates the consequence over time ('Within a year'). S concludes ('Consequently, periodic refactoring...'). Order: Q-P-R-S.
questions.shortcut: Look for 'this immediate speed gain' in P referring back to 'Rapid prototyping' in Q.

questions.question: Choose the grammatically cleanest replacement for the underlined part: 'Having reviewed the crash logs thoroughly, [the memory leak was traced by the team to] an unclosed database cursor.'
options: the memory leak was traced by the team to
the team traced the memory leak to
it was traced by the team that the memory leak came from
tracing the memory leak was done by the team to
questions.explanation: The opening participial phrase 'Having reviewed the crash logs thoroughly' must modify the grammatical subject immediately following the comma. Since 'the team' reviewed the logs (not 'the memory leak'), 'the team traced the memory leak to' fixes the dangling modifier.
questions.shortcut: Who reviewed the crash logs? 'The team'—so 'the team' must immediately follow the comma.

questions.question: Select the option that best fills the blanks: 'Although the incident post-mortem began with ______ exchanges between teams, the director's data-driven summary steered the meeting toward ______ resolution.'
questions.explanation: 'Although' signals a contrast between the tense opening and the productive outcome. 'Acrimonious' (bitter/angry) contrasts naturally with 'constructive' (helpful/productive).
questions.shortcut: 'Although' demands opposite tones: negative opening (acrimonious) vs positive ending (constructive).

questions.question: Identify the erroneous segment: 'The new compliance policy (A) / is markedly different than (B) / the guidelines issued (C) / by the regional board last quarter. (D)'
questions.explanation: In standard formal English tested in placement assessments, the adjective 'different' takes the preposition 'from' ('different from'), not 'different than' before a simple noun phrase.
questions.shortcut: Standard idiom check: 'different from' (not 'different than' before a noun phrase).

questions.question:
Arrange P, Q, R, S in logical order:
P. Such bias is rarely intentional; rather, it stems from historical under-representation in training records.
Q. Automated resume screeners promise faster shortlisting for campus recruitment drives.
R. Auditing model outputs against diverse candidate cohorts therefore becomes indispensable.
S. Yet when trained purely on past hiring decisions, they risk amplifying latent demographic skews.
questions.explanation: Q introduces resume screeners. S introduces the caveat ('Yet... latent demographic skews'). P refers directly to 'Such bias'. R draws the final recommendation ('therefore becomes indispensable'). Order: Q-S-P-R.
questions.shortcut: 'Such bias' in P points to 'latent demographic skews' in S, giving S-P.

questions.question: Select the best correction: 'If the build pipeline [would have executed] the integration suite earlier, the regression would never have reached staging.'
questions.explanation: In a third conditional (unreal past condition + 'would have + past participle' in the main clause), the 'if' clause requires the past perfect tense: 'had executed'.
questions.shortcut: Third conditional rule: If + had + V3, ... would have + V3.

questions.question: Argument: 'Switching our enterprise portal from server-rendered pages to a single-page architecture reduced average page-transition latency by 40%, proving the rewrite improved overall user productivity.' Which statement, if true, most WEAKENS this conclusion?
options: Backend API throughput remained stable throughout the migration window
Initial cold-load time tripled on mobile networks, causing 35% of field agents to abandon sessions before the first screen loaded
Frontend developers required three weeks of training on the new component framework
Browser caching headers were updated two months prior to the rewrite
questions.explanation: While transitions between pages got faster, if initial load time tripled and 35% of users abandoned sessions before even reaching the first screen, overall user productivity clearly did not improve.
questions.shortcut: Look for a hidden cost (35% session abandonment on initial load) that outweighs page-transition gains.
